- Deleting files (no rm or deletion)
- Moving or copying files (no mv or cp)
- Creating temporary files anywhere, including /tmp
- Using redirect operators (>, >>, |) or heredocs to write to files
- Running ANY commands that change system state

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

Your strengths:
- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns
- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

Guidelines:
- Use `find` via Bash for broad file pattern matching
- Use `grep` via Bash for searching file contents with regex
- Use Read when you know the specific file path you need to read
- Use Bash ONLY for read-only operations (ls, git status, git log, git diff, find, grep, cat, head, tail)
- NEVER use Bash for: mkdir, touch, rm, cp, mv, git add, git commit, npm install, pip install, or any file creation/modification
- Adapt your search approach based on the thoroughness level specified by the caller
- Communicate your final report directly as a regular message - do NOT attempt to create files

NOTE: You are meant to be a fast agent that returns output as quickly as possible. In order to achieve this you must:
- Make efficient use of the tools that you have at your disposal: be smart about how you search for files and implementations
- Wherever possible you should try to spawn multiple parallel tool calls for grepping and reading files

Complete the user's search request efficiently and report your findings clearly.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

7	 *
8	 * Used by: URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic,

10	 *
11	 * When adding a country:
12	 *   1. Add it to config/sites.overlay.js (and e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js

26	/**
27	 * Who owns checkout for this site's domestic path.
28	 * For HK and ME, Global-e always owns checkout AND pricing from PDP onward.
29	 * For AU, US, GB, EU: SFCC owns domestic paths; Global-e takes over when the
30	 * user's shipping destination is outside the site's domestic market.
31	 */
32	export type CheckoutOwner = 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';
33	
34	export type CountryConfig = {
35	  /** URL path segment, e.g. 'au', 'us', 'fr-eu' */
36	  urlSlug: string;
37	  /** The real SFCC site this locale routes to */
38	  sfccSiteId: string;
39	  /** IETF locale used by PWA Kit / SFCC, e.g. 'en-AU' */
40	  locale: string;
41	  /** ISO 4217 currency code */
42	  currency: string;
43	  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 shipping/tax country */
44	  shippingCountry: string;
45	  /**
46	   * Checkout owner for this site's domestic path.
47	   * Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level —
48	   * not only at the checkout page.
49	   */
50	  checkoutOwner: CheckoutOwner;
51	  /**
52	   * When true, Global-e owns pricing, currency, and tax display from PDP
53	   * onward — do not render SFCC prices on these paths.
54	   */
55	  globalEPricing: boolean;
56	  /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */
57	  boutiqueRegion: string;
58	};
59	
60	type CountryOverlayEntry = Pick<
61	  CountryConfig,
62	  'shippingCountry' | 'checkoutOwner' | 'globalEPricing' | 'boutiqueRegion'
63	>;

66	 * Hand-maintained business/geo data, keyed the same way as
67	 * countries.generated.ts (URL slug; 'au' for the root/default site).
68	 *
69	 * 'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no
70	 * matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet — it's excluded from the
71	 * final COUNTRIES export below until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to
72	 * config/sites.overlay.js (pending BM confirmation of the real site ID —
73	 * see .docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md).
74	 */
75	const COUNTRY_OVERLAY: Record<string, CountryOverlayEntry> = {
76	  au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' },
77	  us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' },
78	  'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl
79	  uk: { shippingCountry: 'GB', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'uk' },
80	  'en-eu': { shippingCountry: 'DE', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
81	  'fr-eu': { shippingCountry: 'FR', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' },
82	  'it-eu': { shippingCountry: 'IT', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
83	  'es-eu': { shippingCountry: 'ES', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
84	  'en-ch': { shippingCountry: 'CH', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; Global-e resolves shipping country
85	  hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' },
86	  'en-ae': { shippingCountry: 'AE', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'middle-east' },

91	 * AU is the exception: it has no URL prefix (root domain). Its key is 'au'
92	 * but urlSlug is '' — routing falls back to DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG when no

96	// matching business-logic overlay — that means someone added a site to
97	// config/sites.overlay.js and ran `npm run sync:regional-config` without

99	// (an overlay entry with no generated data yet, e.g. 'en-ca' pending the

101	const missingOverlays = Object.keys(GENERATED_COUNTRIES).filter((slug) => !(slug in COUNTRY_OVERLAY));

112	    .map(([slug, overlay]) => [

126	export const COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
127	  Object.values(COUNTRIES).map((c) => [c.shippingCountry, c]),

2	// Design System 2026 Figma (node wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/40003890:151736 and /40003890:151742,
3	// audited 2026-09-16). Divider colour resolves to `alias/color/border/secondary` in Figma
4	// which binds to `#dddddd` — surfaced in this codebase as
5	// `--zimm-color-border-tertiary` (see foundation/colour.ts `border.tertiary`). Figma's N+1
6	// divider pattern (7 dividers for 6 accordions: top + between + bottom) is reproduced by
7	// giving each item both `borderTop` and `borderBottom`, with no `_first`/`_last` override.
8	
9	export const ZimmAccordion = {
10	  parts: ['root', 'item', 'header', 'label', 'alwaysVisible', 'panel'],
11	  baseStyle: {
12	    root: {
13	      width: '100%',
14	    },
15	    // Every item carries both top and bottom borders so the accordion group reads as N+1
16	    // dividers between headers, matching Figma. Chakra's own AccordionItem defaults are
17	    // overridden here rather than layered on: the default `1px solid` uses the theme border
18	    // colour, not the drawer-specific tertiary token.
19	    item: {
20	      borderTop: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-tertiary)',
21	      borderBottom: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-tertiary)',
22	      // Collapse the shared edge between adjacent items so a single 1px line renders instead
23	      // of a doubled 2px seam. Only the last item keeps its own borderBottom.
24	      _notLast: {
25	        borderBottom: 'none',
26	      },
27	    },
28	    // Chakra's AccordionButton is a real <button>; these sx overrides layer over its defaults
29	    // (transparent bg, blackAlpha _hover, block layout). Cursor: pointer stays Chakra-owned.
30	    // paddingBlock 20px per row yields ~41px between adjacent header baselines (20 + 1px
31	    // border + 20), matching Figma's `Accordion group` gap-with-divider rhythm.
32	    header: {
33	      display: 'flex',
34	      alignItems: 'center',
35	      justifyContent: 'space-between',
36	      width: '100%',
37	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)',
38	      paddingInline: 0,
39	      _hover: {
40	        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
41	      },
42	      _focusVisible: {
43	        // audit-allow: 2px matches Chakra's default focus-ring outline width; no dedicated
44	        // Zimmermann token for outline width (only offset + composite).
45	        outline: '2px solid var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
46	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
47	      },
48	    },
49	    label: {
50	      // textTransform intentionally NOT set here — `textStyle="productNames"` (applied in
51	      // index.tsx) already carries `textTransform: 'uppercase'` from the design system.
52	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
53	      flex: '1 0 0',
54	      textAlign: 'left',
55	    },
56	    // Rendered directly below the header regardless of expanded state. Padding matches the
57	    // panel's so a facet's chips align visually with the options list below when expanded.
58	    alwaysVisible: {
59	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
60	      paddingInline: 0,
61	    },
62	    panel: {
63	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
64	      paddingInline: 0,
65	      // Constrain children to available width. Without this, Stack/Flex children can expand
66	      // beyond the drawer's bounds, causing horizontal overflow (audited 2026-09-16: Stack
67	      // was 634px on 375px viewport). Width 100% + border-box ensures children don't exceed
68	      // their parent's computed width.
69	      width: '100%',
70	      boxSizing: 'border-box',
71	      overflow: 'hidden',
72	    },
73	  },
74	};

3	// SFCC-847 drawer/content/filters — organism layout recipe. Matches the Zimmermann Design
4	// System 2026 Figma `content-container` semantics (node wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/40003890:151736
5	// and /40003890:151742, audited 2026-09-16): paddingInline 64px, paddingBlock 48px, and a
6	// 64px column gap between the accordion body and the CLEAR/APPLY button-group. No border
7	// separator between body and footer — the gap alone provides the visual break in Figma.
8	//
9	// Layout intent (confirmed by Figma node 40003890:151730 audit 2026-09-21): content-container
10	// is `shrink-0` in Figma — it flows naturally with its content rather than filling the drawer
11	// to the bottom. Buttons appear immediately after the accordion group (64px gap), with
12	// whitespace below in the collapsed state. The parent ZimmDrawer wrapper owns `overflow-y: auto`
13	// so the entire content area (accordions + buttons) scrolls together when expanded content
14	// overflows the panel height.
15	
16	export const ZimmFiltersDrawerContent = {
17	  parts: ['root', 'body', 'footer'],
18	  baseStyle: {
19	    root: {
20	      display: 'flex',
21	      flexDirection: 'column',
22	      // Flows naturally with content (Figma content-container is shrink-0, not height-filled).
23	      // The ZimmDrawer wrapper owns the scroll — do not claim height: 100% here.
24	      width: '100%',
25	      // Explicit border-box sizing ensures padding never causes overflow beyond the available width.
26	      boxSizing: 'border-box',
27	      // 64px column gap between accordion body and CLEAR/APPLY footer, matching Figma
28	      // content-container `gap: var(--alias/space/1600, 64px)`. Replaces the earlier
29	      // borderTop separator on the footer — Figma has no separator here.
30	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)',
31	      // Responsive padding: 16px (--zimm-scale-m) at mobile; 64px (--zimm-scale-4xl) at desktop/tablet.
32	      // Mobile drawer collapses to full viewport height, so large padding causes left-edge overflow.
33	      // Audited 2026-09-16: 16px on both sides = 32px total, leaves ~343px on 375px mobile viewport
34	      // for accordion content — sufficient for label + checkbox.
35	      paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-m)',
36	      paddingBlock: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
37	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
38	        paddingInline: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)',
39	      },
40	    },
41	    body: {
42	 
43	      //
44	      // No overflowX here, deliberately. It was `hidden`, which made this element's padding
45	      // box the horizontal clip rect — and with no paddingInline of its own (the 64px lives on
46	      // `root`, outside this element) that clip edge sat flush against the accordion, cutting
47	      // the left side of the ZimmSelectedChip focus ring, which paints outside its border box
48	      // via --zimm-focus-ring-offset-*. It was originally added for a Stack measuring 634px on
49	      // a 375px viewport, but width:100% + minWidth:0 below is what actually lets flex children
50	      // shrink. If horizontal scroll returns on mobile, constrain the offending child instead —
51	      // restoring overflowX here would clip the focus ring again.
52	      //
53	      // Constrain width to prevent children (accordion, stacks) from expanding beyond bounds.
54	      // Audited 2026-09-16: even with accordion panel width constraints, Stack was still
55	      // 634px on 375px viewport, causing pale stripe on left. Adding width + minWidth: 0
56	      // allows flex children to shrink properly.
57	      width: '100%',
58	      minWidth: 0,
59	      boxSizing: 'border-box',
60	    },
61	    // CLEAR/APPLY action row. Owns its own layout rather than delegating to a separate
62	    // button-group component — the same pattern zimmModal.css.ts's ZimmModal recipe uses for
63	    // its `actions` part. Stacked full-width on mobile (Figma node 40003890:151809), inline
64	    // and equal-width from tablet up (node 40003890:151736).
65	    footer: {
66	      flexShrink: 0,
67	      display: 'flex',
68	      width: '100%',
69	      flexDirection: 'column',
70	      // 16px between CLEAR and APPLY — Figma `alias/space/400`.
71	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-m)',
72	      '& > *': {
73	        flex: 'none',
74	        width: '100%',
75	        minWidth: 0,
76	      },
77	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
78	        flexDirection: 'row',

80	        '& > *': {

84	        },
85	      },

# PRD – Regional Storefronts, Consent & Routing

_Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13)._

---

## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).

> **Status (2026-07-10):** REG-005 is **updated** — the US is now **two separate SFCC sites**: a US domestic site (`/us/`, SFCC checkout only) and a US international site (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout only). This supersedes the 2026-06-11 single-site decision. Rationale: managing Global-e complexity is simpler with a dedicated site boundary; inventory pooling and reporting can be handled at the SFCC realm level. **New site IDs require confirmation in Business Manager** — `ZimmermannUSIntl` is the working name for the international site.

Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).

11 active locales across the 8 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international remain separate storefronts (REG-006). US domestic and US international are now separate storefronts (REG-005, updated 2026-07-10).

SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):

| Locale           | SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                     | URL prefix                     | Local currency         | Checkout owner          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| AU (+ Oceania)   | `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                             | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD                    | SFCC (REG-003)          |
| UK               | `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                          | `/uk/`                         | GBP                    | SFCC (REG-004)          |
| US domestic      | `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                          | `/us/`                         | USD                    | SFCC (REG-005)          |
| US international | `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(confirm locale in BM)_ | `/en-ca/`                      | USD                    | Global-e (REG-005)      |
| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB`                          | `/en-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC (REG-006 dom)      |
| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `fr`                             | `/fr-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `it`                             | `/it-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU`             | `es`                             | `/es-eu/`                      | EUR                    | SFCC                    |
| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                          | `/en-ch/`                      | EUR                    | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK               | `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                          | `/hk/`                         | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007)      |
| ME               | `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                          | `/en-ae/`                      | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008)      |

ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).

URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).

Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).

The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).

### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:

- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.

**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).

> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.

---

## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)

When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):

- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)

Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

---

## 3. Checkout Ownership

- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

_For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md)._

---

## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)

- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

---

# SFCC-801 Inventory — Country/Currency Selector

## DATA

### 1. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/config/countries.ts`

**FLAT map, keyed by URL slug. NOT grouped by region.** It's a derived merge of an auto-generated SCAPI file plus a hand-maintained business overlay.

Exact exported type:

```ts
export type CheckoutOwner = 'sfcc' | 'global-e' | 'hybrid';

export type CountryConfig = {
  urlSlug: string;        // 'us', 'fr-eu'; '' for AU (root)
  sfccSiteId: string;     // 'ZimmermannUS'
  locale: string;         // 'en-US'
  currency: string;       // 'USD'
  shippingCountry: string;// 'US' — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
  checkoutOwner: CheckoutOwner;
  globalEPricing: boolean;
  boutiqueRegion: string;
};
```

Exports: `COUNTRIES: Record<string, CountryConfig>`, `DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG = 'au'`, `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE: Record<string, CountryConfig>`.

Sample overlay entries (verbatim, lines 76-86):
```ts
au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' },
us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' },
hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' },
```

The locale/currency half comes from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` (`GENERATED_COUNTRIES`), e.g.:
```ts
us: { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannUS', locale: 'en-US', currency: 'USD' },
'fr-eu': { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locale: 'fr', currency: 'EUR' },
'en-ae': { sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannME', locale: 'en-AE', currency: 'EUR' },
```

**Gaps for SFCC-801, blunt:**
- **No display name field.** There is no `"United States"` / `"Hong Kong"` string anywhere. `shippingCountry` is a 2-letter code only. You must author display names (or wire `Intl.DisplayNames`).
- **No flag reference field.**
- **No region field** in the SFCC-801 sense. `boutiqueRegion` exists but its values are `australia | usa | uk | europe | hong-kong | middle-east` — a boutique-locator filter key, one-per-storefront, not "Europe / Asia Pacific / Americas". AU and US each get their own bucket; it does not group.
- `'en-ca'` (Canada/US-International) is **filtered out** of `COUNTRIES` at runtime (line 111) because `ZimmermannUSIntl` isn't in `config/sites.overlay.js` yet. So `COUNTRIES` has **10** entries, not 11.
- Currency drift you must decide on: `countries.generated.ts` says HK = `USD` and ME = `EUR`, but `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/regional.md` line 32-33 says HK = **HKD** and ME = **AED** (via SFCC price books). If the drawer shows a currency code, these two are contradictory sources.

### 2. Sites & l10n

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.js` is a merge function only — it maps `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-written) over `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI). **11 PWA sites.** Every PWA site has exactly **one** locale (that locale is its `defaultLocale`) and **one** currency.

| PWA site id | sfccSiteId | locale | alias / URL prefix | supportedCurrencies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ZimmermannAU` | — | `en` | *(none — root `/`)* | `['AUD']` |
| `ZimmermannUS` | — | `en-US` | `us` | `['USD']` |
| `ZimmermannUSIntl` | — | `en-CA` | `en-ca` | `['USD']` |
| `ZimmermannUK` | — | `en-GB` | `uk` | `['GBP']` |
| `ZimmermannEUen` | `ZimmermannEU` | `en-GB` | `en-eu` | `['EUR']` |
| `ZimmermannEUfr` | `ZimmermannEU` | `fr` | `fr-eu` | `['EUR']` |
| `ZimmermannEUit` | `ZimmermannEU` | `it` | `it-eu` | `['EUR']` |
| `ZimmermannEUes` | `ZimmermannEU` | `es` | `es-eu` | `['EUR']` |
| `ZimmermannEUIntl` | — | `en-CH` | `en-ch` | `['EUR']` |
| `ZimmermannHK` | — | `en-HK` | `hk` | `['USD']` |
| `ZimmermannME` | — | `en-AE` | `en-AE`→alias `en-ae` | `['EUR']` |

URL prefix scheme — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/default.js`:
- `app.url.site: 'path'`, `app.url.locale: 'path'`, `app.url.showDefaults: false`
- `app.defaultSite: 'ZimmermannAU'`
- `app.siteAliases` (line 125): the alias table above. AU deliberately has no alias → serves at root.

**Critical for the "language selector" section:** `supportedCurrencies` is a single-element array on every site, and each PWA site carries exactly **one** locale. So the EU EN/FR/IT/ES language choice is **not** a locale switch within one site — it is a **site switch** across four PWA sites. Currency is never user-selectable; it is derived from the chosen country. Your `onConfirm(country, locale)` must therefore resolve to `(targetAlias, targetLocale)` and hard-navigate.

### 3. Region grouping — DEFINITIVE: does not exist in code. Must be authored.

`grep` for `region|REGIONS|Europe|Asia Pacific|Americas` across `overrides/`, `config/`, `scripts/`:
- `region` in this codebase means **Contentful region = one siteId**. See `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`, `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/types/contentful.ts` (`RegionEntry`), `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs` (`REGION_SEEDS` — one entry per site, e.g. `{ siteId: 'ZimmermannME', label: 'Middle East', locale: 'en-AE' }`).
- `boutiqueRegion` in `countries.ts` — store-locator filter key, one per storefront.
- Zero occurrences of `'Asia Pacific'`, `'Americas'`, or a geographic-region→countries map anywhere in `overrides/` or `config/`.

**The requirement does exist in the PRD but only in prose.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.docs/prd/regional.md`:
- Line 65 (REG-021): *"Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field."* Note the PRD says **three** regions and also mandates a **search field** — the ticket description you gave me omits search.
- Lines 45-56 hold the full country→storefront prose lists (AU/Oceania ~19 countries, EU domestic ~30, EU intl ~60 incl. all Africa, HK ~28, ME ~10, US-intl ~35). That is the raw material, but it is prose in a markdown doc, not data.
- Line 65 also: selector **not available on AU** (REG-020/REG-025). Line 67-68: China→HK, Australia-from-elsewhere→HK (REG-026/027).

**Verdict: the region→countries mapping is a build-from-scratch data authoring item**, and you need a product decision on whether the list is 10 storefronts grouped into 3 regions, or ~190 shipping destinations grouped into 3 regions.

### 4. Adjacent organisms

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/index.tsx` (SFCC-831)
- A two-variant **prompt/interstitial**, not a picker. `ZimmDrawer size="prompt"` + `labelledBy` + `boxedHeader`.
- Props: discriminated union on `variant: 'location' | 'language'`; base `{ isOpen, onDismiss }`; location adds `{ inCountry, currentStore, targetStore, target: unknown, onRedirect }`; language adds `{ inCountry, inLanguage, inCurrentLanguage, target: unknown, onSwitchLanguage }`.
- Renders exactly: heading + paragraph + two `ZimmButton`s. **No list, no radio, no accordion, no flags.**
- Reads **no** data source — deliberately "ignorant of sites/locales/aliases"; `target` is opaque and echoed back.
- **Solves ~0% of SFCC-801's picker.** Its real value is as the *precedent pattern*: opaque-target callback contract, `useUiCopy` copy-key table, drawer composition, and the `boxedHeader` prop. Note its location variant's CTA #2 in the PRD (REG-016) is "open the country selector" — so **SFCC-801 is this component's missing counterpart**, and there is currently no wiring between them.

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmLanguagePrompt/index.tsx` (SFCC-689)
- Container that mounts the above. Props: `{ site: {id, sfccSiteId?}, locale: {id}, buildUrl }`.
- Contains `EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG` — the **only existing language-label data in the repo**: `en → {alias:'en-eu', locale:'en-GB', 'in English'}`, `fr → {'fr-eu','fr','in French'}`, `it`, `es`. Directly reusable as the EU language-section source.
- Establishes the navigation contract you should copy verbatim: **write suppression cookie synchronously, then `window.location.href = crossSiteUrl(alias, locale, buildUrl)`** — never a client-side route change, because a site switch changes the Commerce API siteId/basket/locale resolved at boot.
- Mounted at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:511`.

### 5. Base Salesforce locale selector

- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/partials/` contains **only** `above-header.jsx`. No selector there.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/locale-selector/index.jsx` — a nested Chakra `Accordion` disclosure. Props: `{ selectedLocale, locales: string[], onSelect }`. Has a hardcoded `flags` map (`'en-GB'`, `'fr-FR'`, `'it-IT'`, `'zh-CN'`, `'ja-JP'`). Selection indicator is a `CheckIcon`, **not a radio**. No currency, no region grouping, no confirm footer.
